examples.en: The sky suddenly darkened and then it rained.
A message came all of a sudden, so I postponed the plan.
My father suddenly decided to move.

examples.ko: 급작스레 찾아온 손님 때문에 정신이 없었어요.
examples.en: I was flustered because of the guest who showed up out of the blue.
The weather turned cold suddenly, so I caught a cold.

examples.ko: 친구가 급작스레 유학을 가겠다고 해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised when my friend suddenly said they'd study abroad.

explain: '갑자기'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 글 같은 느낌이고, 예상 못 한 일이 닥친 느낌이 조금 더 강해요. 보통 말할 때는 '갑자기'를 훨씬 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The schedule changed all of a sudden.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급작스레'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 이 형태가 조금 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 급작스레, and this form sounds a bit more natural in speech.

phrases.en: It suddenly rained, and I had no umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 흔히 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common, easy word in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The weather changed suddenly, so I caught a cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상하지 못하게 상황이 달라질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for when a situation changes unexpectedly.

explain_en: It is similar to '갑자기' but sounds more written and slightly stronger in the sense of something unexpected hitting. In everyday speech, '갑자기' is used much more.

en: dead of night; middle of the night

examples.ko: 오밤중에 갑자기 전화가 와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A phone call came in the dead of night and I was startled.
I want to eat ramyeon in the middle of the night.
Where are you going at this hour of the night?
It was noisy until the dead of night, so I couldn't sleep.
The child woke up in the middle of the night and cried.
It's the dead of night, so the buses have stopped running.

explain: '한밤중'과 같은 시간이지만 입말 느낌이 강해요. 늦은 시간에 놀랍거나 못마땅할 때 '이 오밤중에'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I woke up hungry in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 시간을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used with '에' to mark the time.
phrases.en_equiv: in the middle of the night

phrases.en: Where are you going at this hour of the night?
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 못마땅한 마음을 담아 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a tone of surprise or disapproval.

phrases.en: It rained a lot in the dead of night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '오밤중'보다 덜 입말 같고 글에서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but less colloquial and also used in writing.

explain_en: It refers to the same time as '한밤중' but sounds more colloquial. People often use it as '이 오밤중에' when surprised or annoyed at the late hour.

examples.en: It's the day before the exam, so every minute and second is precious.

examples.ko: 그는 일분일초도 허투루 쓰지 않고 공부했어요.
examples.en: He studied without wasting a single minute or second.
In the emergency room, there are many cases where every second counts.

examples.ko: 일분일초에 승패가 갈리는 경기라 손에 땀이 났어요.
examples.en: It was a match decided by the minute and second, so my palms were sweaty.

examples.ko: 공연 시작을 기다리는 동안 일분일초마다 긴장이 커졌어요.
examples.en: While waiting for the show to start, my nerves grew with every passing moment.

examples.ko: 합격 발표를 기다리는 일분일초가 너무 길게 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: Every minute of waiting for the results felt way too long.

explain: '일 분 일 초'처럼 아주 짧은 시간도 놓치지 않는다는 느낌으로, 시간이 아깝거나 급하거나 긴장될 때 써요. '일분일초가 아깝다', '일분일초도 ~지 않다'처럼 말해요. 가볍게는 '1분 1초'라고 숫자로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: For an emergency patient, every second counts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금만 늦어도 결과가 달라질 만큼 시간이 급할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when time is so tight that even a slight delay changes the outcome.
phrases.en_equiv: be a race against time; every second counts

explain_en: It carries the feeling that not even a single minute or second can be missed, used when time is precious, urgent or tense. People say '일분일초가 아깝다' or '일분일초도 ~지 않다'. In casual writing it can also be written with numbers, '1분 1초'.

en: to stay up all night; to sit up all night

examples.en: I stayed up all night the night before the exam.
I ended up staying up all night talking with a friend.

examples.ko: 월드컵 경기를 보며 밤을 지새우는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people stay up all night watching World Cup games.
I lie awake all night because of worry.

examples.ko: 밤을 지새우면 다음 날 너무 피곤해요.
examples.en: If you stay up all night, you're very tired the next day.

examples.ko: 오늘은 밤을 지새울 각오로 공부할 거예요.
examples.en: Today I'm going to study ready to stay up all night.

explain: 거의 '밤을 지새우다'처럼 '밤'과 함께 써요. '밤을 새우다'와 비슷하지만 조금 글 같은 말투예요. '지새워요/지새웠어요'로 활용해요.

phrases.en: I was worried, so I stayed up all night without sleeping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한숨도 못 자고 밤을 보냈다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you spent the night without sleeping at all.
phrases.en_equiv: to stay up all night awake

phrases.en: I have had many sleepless nights because of exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거를 꾸미는 형태로 '잠 못 잔 밤'을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A past modifier meaning a night without sleep.

phrases.en: I stayed up all night because of homework yesterday.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in everyday speech than 지새우다.

explain_en: It is almost always used with '밤', as in '밤을 지새우다'. It is close to '밤을 새우다' but sounds a little more literary. It conjugates as '지새워요/지새웠어요'.

examples.en: The second hand of the clock keeps going round without stopping.

examples.ko: 초침 소리 때문에 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I can't sleep because of the sound of the second hand.
I timed it while watching the second hand.

examples.ko: 이 시계는 초침 없이 조용히 움직여요.
examples.en: This clock moves quietly with no second hand.
It's the moment the second hand and minute hand overlap.
The second hand moves faster than the minute hand.

explain: 시계의 바늘 이름으로 '시침, 분침, 초침'을 같이 외워 두세요. 초침이 소리를 내는 시계 이야기에서 '초침 소리'라는 말이 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 시계 초침이 멈췄어요. 건전지를 바꿔야 해요.
phrases.en: The clock's second hand stopped. I need to change the battery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시계가 고장 났거나 건전지가 다 됐을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a clock is broken or the battery is dead.

phrases.en: I watched the second hand, waiting for the exam to end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기다리는 시간이 길게 느껴질 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits moments when waiting feels long.

phrases.en: The hour hand is short and the minute hand is long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시계 바늘을 함께 설명할 때 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said together when explaining clock hands.

explain_en: Learn the clock hand names together: '시침' (hour hand), '분침' (minute hand) and '초침' (second hand). In talk about ticking clocks, the phrase '초침 소리' (sound of the second hand) comes up often.

en: to be longtime; to be long-lasting

examples.en: I work overtime day after day, so I'm exhausted.
My brother does nothing but play games all the time.

examples.ko: 허구한 날 늦는 친구를 기다리기 지쳤어요.
examples.en: I'm tired of waiting for a friend who is late every single day.

examples.ko: 허구한 날 비가 와서 빨래를 못 말려요.
examples.en: It rains day after day, so I can't dry my laundry.

examples.ko: 왜 허구한 날 같은 반찬만 먹어요?
examples.en: Why do we eat the same side dishes every single day?

examples.ko: 허구한 날 싸우는 부부를 보면 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts to see a couple who argue day after day.

explain: 거의 항상 '허구한 날'이라는 덩어리로만 쓰고, 불평하는 느낌이 들어요. '매일'은 그냥 사실을 말하지만, '허구한 날'은 지겹고 짜증 난다는 마음이 들어가 있어요. 혼자 '허구해요'라고 말하는 일은 거의 없어요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 허구한 날 약속에 늦어요.
phrases.en: That friend is late for appointments all the time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늘 반복되는 나쁜 습관에 불만을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to complain about a bad habit that keeps repeating.

phrases.en: The brothers fight all the time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지겹게 계속되는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that goes on tiresomely.

phrases.en: My younger sibling wakes up late every single day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허구한 날'과 비슷하지만 불평하는 느낌이 덜해서 더 쓰기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 허구한 날 but less of a complaint, so it is easier to use.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the fixed chunk '허구한 날' and carries a complaining tone. 매일 just states a fact, while 허구한 날 adds the feeling of being fed up. People hardly ever say '허구해요' alone.
